The pacing of the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the emotional weight of the narrative. The story takes place over a very short span of "story time"—just the few minutes it takes to dock a ferry and walk up to a house. However, the author skillfully stretches brief moments (such as Jonas losing his balance on the planks, a simple nod, or the smell of old coffee) by weaving in Ilse's internal reflections and memories. At the same time, years of backstory—Jonas growing up and becoming estranged, and the death of Henning—are compressed into single, poignant sentences (e.g., the four boots under the canopy, the leftover coffee). Meanwhile, the physical transition from the ferry dock to the garden fence and into the hallway is compressed smoothly without unnecessary filler, keeping the story grounded in the quiet, tense rhythm of their reunion.
